userStories.title: Thread scope; project thread surfaces never expose a WORKSPACE thread
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the thread repository's bare `projectId` with a `ThreadScope` so project thread routes exclude WORKSPACE rows and workspace-scope reads are creator-only, and make `findThreadTokenScope` report WORKSPACE.

**Motivation** — A PROJECT-visible surface must never serve a WORKSPACE thread (1d-D7, S5b-R12); the transcript is only safe if every shared lookup is scoped.

**Approach**
- `ThreadScope` — new, in `chat-thread.domain.ts`:
```ts
/** Which threads a lookup may see: a project's REPO and PROJECT threads, or one user's WORKSPACE threads. */
export type ThreadScope = { kind: 'project'; projectId: string } | { kind: 'workspace'; userId: string };
```
The repository turns it into a Prisma `where` fragment: `project` → `{ projectId, kind: { not: 'WORKSPACE' } }`; `workspace` → `{ createdById: userId, kind: 'WORKSPACE' }`. A `workspace`-scope `list` or `get` also reads each thread's home project (`project: { select: { slug: true, name: true } }`, soft-deleted projects included) into `homeProject`.
- `ChatThreadRepository` (`chat-thread.domain.ts:93-107`) and `PrismaChatThreadRepository` — Baseline: `list(projectId, …)`, `get(projectId, id)`, `updateCap(projectId, …)`, `command(projectId, …)`, `archive(projectId, …)`, `sendMessage({ projectId, … })`. Target: each takes `scope: ThreadScope` in place of `projectId` (`sendMessage`'s input field becomes `scope`), and every `chatThread.findFirst` / `findMany` inside them filters by the scope fragment (both the pre-lock and the under-lock reads). `publish(projectId, …)` and `discard(projectId, …)` keep `projectId`; their thread reads gain `kind: { not: 'WORKSPACE' }`. `sendRefusalOf(projectId, thread)`, `handoff`, `messages`, `archivedThreadIds` are unchanged.
- `ThreadsService` (`threads.service.ts`) — public signatures unchanged; each call into the repository passes `{ kind: 'project', projectId }`. This story owns every compile site so the `apps/api` type-check passes after it.
- `ThreadEventsGuard` (`thread-events.controller.ts:26-56`) — Target: the thread read also requires `kind !== 'WORKSPACE'`; a WORKSPACE thread answers `NotFoundAppException({}, 'threads.notFound')` before a stream slot is acquired.
- `IFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts:249`, `prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:216-223`) — Baseline: returns kind `'PROJECT'` or `'REPO'`. Target: returns `{ kind: ChatThreadKind; action: string } | null`, with `WORKSPACE` when the thread row says `WORKSPACE`.
- Test helper `seedThreadJobFor` (`apps/api/test/helpers/thread-fixtures.ts:40-62`) — Target: `SeedThreadOptions` gains optional `kind`, `createdById` and `projectId`; a `WORKSPACE` or `PROJECT` seed writes null `repoId`, `baseRef`, `feature` and `specPath` on the thread (the job keeps `world.repoId` as its anchor). Defaults keep today's REPO seed.
- Existing spec updates: `prisma-chat-thread.repository.spec.ts` calls passing a bare project id — `repo.get('P', 'T')`, `repo.command('P', 'T', 'U', …)`, `sendMessage({ projectId: … })` — become `{ kind: 'project', projectId: 'P' }` scopes; expectations on the Prisma `where` of those reads gain `kind: { not: 'WORKSPACE' }`; behaviour asserted is unchanged. `threads.service.spec.ts:346` (`sendMessage` called with `projectId: 'p1'`) and `:373` (`get` called with `('p1','t1')`) become `scope: { kind: 'project', projectId: 'p1' }` and `get({ kind: 'project', projectId: 'p1' }, 't1')`.

**Scope** — In: ThreadScope, scoped repository methods, ThreadsService call sites, ThreadEventsGuard, findThreadTokenScope, seedThreadJobFor extension. Out: creating WORKSPACE threads and workspace routes (US-003+), consuming `findThreadTokenScope` WORKSPACE in sync/tool route (US-006), any change to `publish`/`discard` signatures.

**Interface**
```ts
export type ThreadScope = { kind: 'project'; projectId: string } | { kind: 'workspace'; userId: string };
// findThreadTokenScope(jobId): Promise<{ kind: ChatThreadKind; action: string } | null>
// SeedThreadOptions gains: kind?: ChatThreadKind; createdById?: string; projectId?: string
```
acceptanceCriteria: With a WORKSPACE thread and a PROJECT thread both stored with `projectId` P, `PrismaChatThreadRepository.list({ kind: 'project', projectId: P }, undefined, 0, 20)` returns the PROJECT thread and not the WORKSPACE thread.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.get({ kind: 'project', projectId: P }, id)` returns null for a WORKSPACE thread stored with `projectId` P.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.get({ kind: 'workspace', userId: U }, id)` returns the WORKSPACE thread whose `createdById` is U, with `homeProject` equal to its project's `slug` and `name`.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.get({ kind: 'workspace', userId: V }, id)` returns null for a WORKSPACE thread whose `createdById` is U.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.get({ kind: 'workspace', userId: U }, id)` returns null for a PROJECT thread whose `createdById` is U.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.list({ kind: 'workspace', userId: U }, undefined, 0, 20)` returns only U's WORKSPACE threads, ordered by `lastActivityAt` descending.
`GET /projects/:slug/threads` by the creator of a WORKSPACE thread whose home project is `:slug` returns no item with that thread's id.
`GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id` for that WORKSPACE thread, requested by its creator who is an ADMIN member of the project, answers 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages` for that WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answers 404 and creates no `ChatMessage` row.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/publish` for that WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answers 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id/events` for that WORKSPACE thread, opened by its creator, answers 404.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/archive` for that WORKSPACE thread, sent by an ADMIN member of the project who did not create it, leaves the thread's `status` `ACTIVE`.
`PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id` with `{ "maxCostUsd": 9 }` for that WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answers 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/end-session` for that WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answers 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`PrismaFleetJobRepository.findThreadTokenScope(jobId)` for the SESSION turn of a thread whose row has `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` returns `{ kind: 'WORKSPACE', action: 'SESSION' }`.

routing.reasoning: Signature change across repository and service with access-control semantics (creator-only visibility, WORKSPACE exclusion on every project surface, pre-lock and under-lock reads); security override applies.

suggestedCriteria: `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/discard` for a WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answers 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/plan` and `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/run` for a WORKSPACE thread, sent by its creator, answer 404 with key `threads.notFound`.
`GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id/events` for a WORKSPACE thread acquires no stream slot.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.list({ kind: 'project', projectId: P }, undefined, 0, 20)` still returns P's REPO and PROJECT threads as before.
`PrismaChatThreadRepository.get({ kind: 'project', projectId: P }, id)` still returns a REPO thread stored with `projectId` P.

modifiedFiles.reason: calls that pass a bare project id — `repo.get('P', 'T')`, `repo.command('P', 'T', 'U', …)` and the `sendMessage({ projectId: … })` inputs — become `{ kind: 'project', projectId: 'P' }` scopes (ruling 1d-D10); expectations on the Prisma `where` of those reads gain `kind: { not: 'WORKSPACE' }`. The behaviour each test asserts is unchanged.

the assertions at `:346` (`sendMessage` called with `projectId: 'p1'`) and `:373` (`get` called with `('p1', 't1')`) become `scope: { kind: 'project', projectId: 'p1' }` and `get({ kind: 'project', projectId: 'p1' }, 't1')`. The service's public signatures are unchanged.
`seedThreadJobFor` gains the optional `kind`, `createdById` and `projectId` seed options described in Design; existing callers keep today's REPO seed.

userStories.title: Create WORKSPACE threads with a home project
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `POST /threads` which creates a WORKSPACE thread for the calling user and books it to a resolved home project.

**Motivation** — The koda assistant must answer across projects, which a PROJECT thread (readable by every project member) cannot do safely; a personal thread needs its own creation path.

**Approach**
- Rulings: **1d-D3 home project.** The *reachable* projects of a user are `ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal(principal)` (non-deleted; a global ADMIN reaches every project). A project can *host* the user's jobs when the user's ability for it — `KodaCaslAbilityFactory.createForUser(withProjectRole(principal, role))`, with `role` from `ProjectAccessService.resolveMembership` — can `CREATE` `FleetJob` (DEVELOPER and above; a global ADMIN everywhere).
  - Default (body has no `homeProject`): the first reachable project, ordered by `createdAt` ascending then `id` ascending, that has a `ProjectMember` row for the user (`ProjectAccessService.findMembershipRole` not null — so a global ADMIN's default is one of the projects they actually belong to, not the oldest project on the system), can host the user's jobs, and has a fleet repo (`IFleetRepoRepository.findAnchor` not null). None → 409 `threads.noFleetRepo`.
  - Explicit `homeProject` slug: not a reachable project's slug (unknown, deleted, or not a member) → 404 `projects`; reachable but cannot host the user's jobs → 403 `threads.homeProjectAccess`; no fleet repo → 409 `threads.noFleetRepo`. Unknown and unreachable answer the same 404, so the route is no project-existence oracle.
  - `ChatThread.projectId` stores the home project. It never changes.
- The kill switch is unchanged: `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` gates WORKSPACE threads exactly as it gates the other kinds.
- `validateCreateWorkspaceThread(value: CreateWorkspaceThreadInput): NormalizedCreateWorkspaceThread` — new, in `thread-input.ts`:
```ts
export interface CreateWorkspaceThreadInput { kind?: ChatThreadKind; repoId?: string; feature?: string; baseRef?: string; homeProject?: string; title: string; maxCostUsd?: number; backend: ThreadBackend }
export interface NormalizedCreateWorkspaceThread { kind: 'WORKSPACE'; homeProject?: string; title: string; maxCostUsd: string; backend: ThreadBackend & { kind: 'native' } }
```
Checks, in order, first failure wins: `kind` (absent or `WORKSPACE`, else reason `kind`); any of `repoId`, `feature`, `baseRef` present (not undefined, not null) → reason `workspaceFields`; `homeProject` absent or null means "default", otherwise it must be a string of 1 to 100 characters, else reason `homeProject`; then the same `title`, `maxCostUsd` (default 5) and `backend` checks as `validateCreateThread`, and a backend of kind `acp` → reason `backend`. All failures are `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'threads.input')` (400).
- `CreateWorkspaceThreadDto` (`dto/workspace-thread.dto.ts`, new) — every field (`kind`, `repoId`, `feature`, `baseRef`, `homeProject`, `title`, `maxCostUsd`, `backend`) carries `@Allow()` as `CreateThreadDto` does (`thread.dto.ts:89-95`), so the global whitelisting pipe keeps `repoId` / `feature` / `baseRef` for the validator to refuse.
- `WorkspaceThreadsService` — new, `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-threads.service.ts`, provided by `ThreadsModule`. `create(principal: UserPrincipal, input: CreateWorkspaceThreadInput): Promise<ChatThreadRecord>`: kill switch (409 `threads.disabled`), validation, home-project resolution (1d-D3), then `ChatThreadRepository.create({ kind: 'WORKSPACE', projectId: home.id, repoId: null, baseRef: null, feature: null, … })` with `skills = SkillsService.snapshotForProject(home.id)`; the result carries `homeProject` = the home project's `{ slug, name }`. `ThreadsModule` imports `ProjectsModule` (for `ProjectsService`; no module cycle — no module behind `ProjectsModule` imports a fleet module) beside the `AuthModule` it already imports for `KodaCaslAbilityFactory`.
- `WorkspaceThreadDto` (`dto/workspace-thread.dto.ts`) — `ThreadDto` plus `@ApiProperty() homeProject: { slug: string; name: string }`. This file also defines `WorkspaceThreadDetailDto` (`ThreadDetailDto` fields plus `homeProject`) and `WorkspaceThreadListDto` (`{ items: WorkspaceThreadDto[]; threadsEnabled: boolean }`); US-004's routes reference them.
- `WorkspaceThreadsController` — new, `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-threads.controller.ts`, `@Controller('threads')`, with `@ApiTags('fleet threads')`, `@ApiBearerAuth()`, and `@ApiOperation` / `@ApiResponse` on every route. Every route answers 403 `threads.principal` to a non-user principal (as `ThreadsController.assertUser`). `POST /threads` → 201 `WorkspaceThreadDto`.
- i18n (`apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json`): new key `homeProjectAccess`.
- Module wiring: `threads.module.spec.ts` gains resolution of `WorkspaceThreadsService` and `WorkspaceThreadsController`; `global-stubs.module.ts` may be extended only if compiling `ThreadsModule` with `ProjectsModule` needs a stub. Run `bun run generate` (openapi.json: POST /api/threads, `CreateWorkspaceThreadDto`, `WorkspaceThreadDto`; CLI types regenerated, never hand-edited).
- Pattern to follow: project create permission check — `ThreadsController.create` (`threads.controller.ts:29-37`).

**Scope** — In: validator, DTOs, create service with home-project resolution, POST /threads, module wiring, i18n key. Out: list/get/messages/events/commands (US-004), send/archive and jobTargetFor (US-005), rate limiting beyond the global throttler.

**Interface**
```ts
export interface CreateWorkspaceThreadInput { kind?: ChatThreadKind; repoId?: string; feature?: string; baseRef?: string; homeProject?: string; title: string; maxCostUsd?: number; backend: ThreadBackend }
export interface NormalizedCreateWorkspaceThread { kind: 'WORKSPACE'; homeProject?: string; title: string; maxCostUsd: string; backend: ThreadBackend & { kind: 'native' } }
export function validateCreateWorkspaceThread(value: CreateWorkspaceThreadInput): NormalizedCreateWorkspaceThread;
// WorkspaceThreadsService.create(principal: UserPrincipal, input: CreateWorkspaceThreadInput): Promise<ChatThreadRecord>
```
acceptanceCriteria: `validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given `kind: 'PROJECT'` throws `ValidationAppException` with key `threads.input` and reason `kind`.
`validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given `repoId: 'r1'` throws `ValidationAppException` with reason `workspaceFields`.
`validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given a backend `{ kind: 'acp', agent: 'claude' }` throws `ValidationAppException` with reason `backend`.
`validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given `homeProject: 42` throws `ValidationAppException` with reason `homeProject`.
`POST /threads` with body `{ "title": "t", "backend": { "kind": "native" }, "repoId": "r1" }` answers 400 with key `threads.input` and reason `workspaceFields`.

`POST /threads` with no `homeProject`, by a user who is a DEVELOPER of project A (created first, with a fleet repo) and of project B (with a fleet repo), answers 201 with `homeProject.slug` equal to A's slug.
The `ChatThread` row created by that request has `kind` `WORKSPACE` and `projectId` equal to A's id.
`POST /threads` with no `homeProject`, by a DEVELOPER of an older project A with no fleet repo and of project B with a fleet repo, answers 201 with `homeProject.slug` equal to B's slug.

`POST /threads` with no `homeProject`, by a user who is a VIEWER of an older project A (with a fleet repo) and a DEVELOPER of project B (with a fleet repo), answers 201 with `homeProject.slug` equal to B's slug.
`POST /threads` with no `homeProject`, by a global ADMIN who has no `ProjectMember` row in any project while a project with a fleet repo exists, answers 409 with key `threads.noFleetRepo`.
`POST /threads` with `homeProject` naming a project where the user is a VIEWER answers 403 with key `threads.homeProjectAccess`.
`POST /threads` with `homeProject` naming a project where the user is a DEVELOPER but which has no fleet repo answers 409 with key `threads.noFleetRepo`.
`POST /threads` with `homeProject` naming an existing project the user is not a member of answers 404 with key `projects`.
`POST /threads` with `homeProject` naming a slug that matches no project answers 404 with key `projects`.
`POST /threads` while `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` is off answers 409 with key `threads.disabled`.

routing.reasoning: New service, controller and DTOs with CASL-based authorization for home-project selection and a no-existence-oracle 404 rule; new module wiring across ProjectsModule; security override applies.

suggestedCriteria: `validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given a 101-character `homeProject` string throws `ValidationAppException` with reason `homeProject`.
`validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given `homeProject: null` returns a result with no `homeProject`.
`validateCreateWorkspaceThread` given no `maxCostUsd` returns `maxCostUsd` `'5'`.
`POST /projects/:slug/threads` with `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` still answers 400 with key `threads.input` and reason `kind`.

userStories.title: WORKSPACE ASSIGN, placement, git tokens, tool route and notices
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make a WORKSPACE THREAD job placeable only on runners advertising `workspaceThreads`, ship it in the ASSIGN without koda tools or project repos, and refuse git tokens and tool calls for it.

**Motivation** — A WORKSPACE ASSIGN must stay off runners that would refuse it with `invalid thread kind`, and the session must never reach project code or koda tools until feature 1d-2.

**Approach**
- Rulings: **1d-D4 capability.** A runner advertises `workspaceThreads: true`; WORKSPACE THREAD jobs are placed only on such runners (misfit `workspace_threads`, recoverable). **1d-D6 no koda tools, no project code.** A WORKSPACE ASSIGN never carries `kodaTools` or `projectRepos`, its session never shows the "koda tools unavailable" notice, and `POST /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/:name` answers 409 `fleet.notThreadJob` for a WORKSPACE thread's job (1d-2 lifts this with the `project` argument). **1d-D8 no git token.** A git-token request without `repoId` for a WORKSPACE THREAD job is refused with reason `repo_not_assigned`; the anchor's token is never minted for it.
- `findThreadAssign` (`prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:224-240`) — Target: `kind` is `WORKSPACE` when the row says `WORKSPACE`, `PROJECT` when it says `PROJECT`, otherwise `REPO`; `feature` keeps `thread.feature ?? thread-<threadId>`.
- `firstMisfit` THREAD branch (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement-rules.ts:118-124`) — Target: right after the `project_threads` check, a job whose `thread.kind` is `WORKSPACE` on a runner whose `capabilities.workspaceThreads !== true` returns the new `MisfitReason` `'workspace_threads'`. Not in `PERMANENT_MISFITS`. Added to `MisfitReason` (`:13`), `PlacementMisfitDto.reason` (`jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts:129`) and the dashboard list (`dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:111`). The credential board's `misfit` enum (`credential-board.dto.ts:42`, fed by `MISFIT_REASONS`) and `AttentionReasonDto` also gain `workspace_threads`.
- `withKodaTools` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement.service.ts:223-226`) — Target: returns the thread unchanged when `thread.kind === 'WORKSPACE'` (1d-D6). `attachProjectRepos` (`:211-214`) already attaches only for `PROJECT`.
- Sync git tokens (`apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync.service.ts:137-140`) — Target: a request without `repoId` for a THREAD job whose `findThreadTokenScope` answers `WORKSPACE` pushes `{ jobId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }` to `gitTokenErrors` and mints nothing.
- `RunnerToolService.call` (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/runner-tool.service.ts:44-52`) — Target: after the `fleet.notThreadJob` check, a job whose `findThreadTokenScope` answers `WORKSPACE` throws `ConflictAppException({}, 'fleet.notThreadJob')` (409); its `jobs` dependency gains `findThreadTokenScope`. `runner-tool.service.spec.ts`'s `jobs` stub gains `findThreadTokenScope` (returning a `PROJECT` scope by default); assertions unchanged.
- `sessionNotices` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/ingest/prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts:477-490`) — Target: a `WORKSPACE` thread never gets `kodaToolsUnavailableOn`.
- Existing spec update: `prisma-fleet-job.repository.find-thread-assign.spec.ts:63-66` ("treats an unknown kind as REPO") uses `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` as its unknown kind; its fixture kind becomes `'FUTURE'`.
- Run `bun run generate` (openapi.json: `PlacementMisfitDto.reason`, `AttentionReasonDto` and the credential board's `misfit` enum gain `workspace_threads`; CLI types regenerated, never hand-edited).
- Patterns: placement misfit — `project_threads` (`placement-rules.ts:123`).

**Scope** — In: findThreadAssign, firstMisfit + MisfitReason surfaces, withKodaTools, sync git-token refusal, RunnerToolService refusal, sessionNotices. Out: runner-side parsing/execution (US-007), koda tools and the `project` argument (feature 1d-2).

**Interface**
```ts
// MisfitReason gains 'workspace_threads' (not in PERMANENT_MISFITS)
// findThreadAssign(jobId): ... kind: 'REPO' | 'PROJECT' | 'WORKSPACE'
// gitTokenErrors entry: { jobId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }
```
acceptanceCriteria: `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findThreadAssign(jobId)` for the THREAD job of a thread whose row has `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` returns `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` and `feature: 'thread-<threadId>'`.
`firstMisfit` for a WORKSPACE THREAD job on an otherwise fitting runner whose capabilities lack `workspaceThreads` returns `'workspace_threads'`.
`firstMisfit` for the same job on a runner whose capabilities have `workspaceThreads: true` and `projectThreads: true` returns no misfit.
`PERMANENT_MISFITS.has('workspace_threads')` returns `false`, so a WORKSPACE THREAD job that fits no runner is left `QUEUED` rather than cancelled.
The generated OpenAPI document's `PlacementMisfitDto` and `AttentionReasonDto` reason enums both contain `workspace_threads`.

The ASSIGN payload `PlacementService` builds for a WORKSPACE SESSION turn on a runner advertising `kodaTools: true` and `projectCode: true` has a `thread` block with neither `kodaTools` nor `projectRepos`.
A runner sync carrying a git-token request without `repoId` for a held WORKSPACE THREAD job answers `gitTokenErrors` containing `{ jobId, reason: 'repo_not_assigned' }` and no git token for that job.
`POST /fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_search_tickets` from the runner holding a RUNNING WORKSPACE THREAD job answers 409 with key `fleet.notThreadJob`.
Thread ingest records no `kodaToolsUnavailableOn` on the session of a WORKSPACE thread whose runner does not advertise `kodaTools`.

After `POST /threads/:id/messages` creates a WORKSPACE THREAD job while the only enabled online runner advertises `projectThreads` but not `workspaceThreads`, `PlacementService.placeJob(jobId)` leaves the job `QUEUED` and returns a misfit list that includes `workspace_threads` for that runner.

After `POST /threads/:id/messages` creates a WORKSPACE THREAD job while an enabled online runner advertises `workspaceThreads`, `projectThreads` and the thread's native model, the job is `ASSIGNED` to that runner and the ASSIGN's `thread.kind` is `WORKSPACE`.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module wiring (placement, ASSIGN, sync git tokens, tool route, ingest notices); git-token minting and runner tool access are credential/access-control paths; security override applies.

suggestedCriteria: `firstMisfit` for a PROJECT THREAD job on a runner that lacks `workspaceThreads` but has `projectThreads: true` returns no misfit.
`RunnerToolService.call` for a PROJECT thread job still dispatches the tool as before.
A runner sync git-token request without `repoId` for a held PROJECT THREAD job is handled as before (no `repo_not_assigned` error from this check).

modifiedFiles.reason: the test at `:63-66` ("treats an unknown kind as REPO") uses `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` as its unknown kind, which `findThreadAssign` now returns as `WORKSPACE`; its fixture kind becomes `'FUTURE'`. US-006 AC-1 is the WORKSPACE counterpart.
regenerated by `bun run generate` for the misfit enum change; never hand-edited.

its `jobs` stub implements the methods `RunnerToolService` used before; it gains `findThreadTokenScope` (returning a `PROJECT` scope by default), because `call` now consults it. Assertions are unchanged.

regenerated with `bun run generate`: `PlacementMisfitDto.reason`, `AttentionReasonDto` and the credential board's `misfit` enum (`credential-board.dto.ts:42`, fed by `MISFIT_REASONS`) gain `workspace_threads`.

outOfScope: koda tools in WORKSPACE threads, the `project` tool argument and `koda_my_projects` (feature 1d-2).
Runner-side parsing and execution (US-007).

userStories.title: Runner accepts and runs WORKSPACE sessions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the Bun runner advertise `workspaceThreads`, accept WORKSPACE ASSIGNs and run them with the no-checkout PROJECT path.

**Motivation** — The API places WORKSPACE THREAD jobs only on runners that advertise the capability; older runners would refuse the kind with `invalid thread kind`.

**Approach**
- `parseAssign` thread block (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:213-216`, `:248`) — Target: accepts kind `WORKSPACE`; a `WORKSPACE` block with an action other than `SESSION` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' }`; `projectRepos` / `projectReposUnavailable` on a `WORKSPACE` block return `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid project repos' }` (unchanged rule: only `PROJECT` may carry them).
- Capability probe (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts:156-175`) — Target: the report gains `workspaceThreads: true`. `nax-probe.spec.ts:85-97` exact report `toEqual` gains `workspaceThreads: true`; warnings and nax-call assertions after it unchanged.
- `ThreadJobRun.run` (`apps/runner/src/thread/thread-job-run.ts:274`) — Target: `thread.kind === 'WORKSPACE'` takes the same `runProject` path as `PROJECT` (no credentials, no worktree, scratch dir `threadScratchDir(homeDir, threadId)`, skill tools only — `projectCodeTools` yields nothing without `projectRepos`).
- `command('THREAD_PUBLISH', …)` (`:890`) — Target: also answers `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_repo_thread' }` for a `WORKSPACE` run.
- The runner imports `ChatThreadKind` from `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` (US-001 adds `WORKSPACE`). Runner tests use bun:test.

**Scope** — In: assign parser, capability probe, ThreadJobRun run branch and THREAD_PUBLISH rejection. Out: all API changes (US-001 to US-006); koda tools or project code for WORKSPACE sessions (feature 1d-2 / out of scope).

**Interface**
```ts
// parseAssign: { ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' } | { ok: false, detail: 'invalid project repos' } for WORKSPACE misuse
// capability report: workspaceThreads: true
// command('THREAD_PUBLISH', ...) on WORKSPACE run -> { result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_repo_thread' }
```
acceptanceCriteria: `parseAssign` for a THREAD ASSIGN whose `thread` block has `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` and `action: 'SESSION'` returns `ok: true` with `assign.thread.kind` equal to `'WORKSPACE'`.
`parseAssign` for a `thread` block with `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` and `action: 'PUBLISH'` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' }`.
`parseAssign` for a `thread` block with `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` that carries `projectRepos` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid project repos' }`.
The capability report the nax probe produces has `workspaceThreads: true`.
`ThreadJobRun.run` for a WORKSPACE SESSION never calls `host.credentials.acquire`.
`ThreadJobRun.run` for a WORKSPACE SESSION opens the session with `worktree` equal to `threadScratchDir(homeDir, threadId)`.
`ThreadJobRun.run` for a WORKSPACE SESSION with no koda tools on the ASSIGN opens the session with exactly the tools named `load_skill` and `read_skill_file`.
`command('THREAD_PUBLISH', …)` on a running WORKSPACE session returns `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'not_repo_thread' }`.

routing.reasoning: Medium because three runner files get small branch additions reusing the existing PROJECT no-checkout path; tdd-simple because nothing here is security-critical and no new abstraction is added.

suggestedCriteria: `parseAssign` for a `thread` block with `kind: 'WORKSPACE'` that carries `projectReposUnavailable` returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid project repos' }`.
`ThreadJobRun.run` for a WORKSPACE SESSION does not create a git worktree.
`parseAssign` for a PROJECT thread block carrying `projectRepos` still returns `ok: true`.

modifiedFiles.reason: the exact report `toEqual` at `:85-97` pins the capability keys; it gains `workspaceThreads: true`. The warnings and nax-call assertions after it are unchanged.

outOfScope: All API changes (US-001 to US-006).

analysis:
Feature 1d-1 of fleet S5b adds a third thread kind, WORKSPACE: a personal thread readable/actable only by its creator (admins included, 1d-D2), served from top-level /threads routes, run on a runner with no checkout (like PROJECT threads) and booked to a home project chosen at creation (1d-D3). API + runner only; web pages, the `project` tool argument and koda_my_projects are feature 1d-2.

KEY FILES (existing):
- packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts:15-16 (ChatThreadKind / CHAT_THREAD_KINDS), :71 ThreadAssign.kind; packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts:76-87 RunnerCapabilities.
- apps/api/src/fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts:13 (API mirror of CHAT_THREAD_KINDS; thread-jobs.spec.ts:32-34 asserts equality with the package export), common/capabilities-core.ts:121-168 (parseCapabilitiesCore; strict `projectThreads` at :141 is the pattern).
- apps/api/src/fleet/runners/dto/runner-summary.dto.ts:26-57 (hasProjectThreads pattern; spec files runner-summary.dto.spec.ts:14, fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts:39-42, test/integration/fleet/runner-views.integration.spec.ts:80 pin the exact key set and must gain workspaceThreads).
- apps/api/src/fleet/threads/: domain/chat-thread.domain.ts (ChatThreadRecord :69-82, repoThreadFields :18-30, ChatThreadRepository :93-107), prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts (mapThreadKind :33, sendRefusalFor :333-352, jobTargetFor :411-429, mapThread :469-481), threads.service.ts, threads.controller.ts (assertUser, create permission check :29-37, list query validation), thread-input.ts (validateCreateThread), thread-instructions.ts (buildProjectThreadInstructions, skillLines), thread-events.controller.ts (ThreadEventsGuard :26-56, ThreadEventsController), threads.module.ts :19-23, dto/thread.dto.ts (ThreadDto :8-31, CreateThreadDto :89-95), ingest/prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts:477-490 (sessionNotices), thread-send-rules.ts:9 (THREAD_MIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION).
- apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/: placement-rules.ts (MisfitReason :13, firstMisfit THREAD branch :118-124, PERMANENT_MISFITS), placement.service.ts (attachProjectRepos :211-214, withKodaTools :223-226), prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts (findThreadTokenScope :216-223, findThreadAssign :224-240), fleet-job.domain.ts:249, dto/fleet-job.dto.ts:129 (PlacementMisfitDto.reason), dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:111, credential-board.dto.ts:42 (MISFIT_REASONS).
- apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync.service.ts:137-140 (git token requests), apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/runner-tool.service.ts:44-52.
- apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.ts:80-90 (findAllForPrincipal), projects/project-access.service.ts:45-80 (resolveMembership, findMembershipRole), projects/project-context.ts (withProjectRole), KodaCaslAbilityFactory (AuthModule).
- apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:213-216,:248; capabilities/nax-probe.ts:156-175; thread/thread-job-run.ts:274 (run kind branch -> runProject), :890 (THREAD_PUBLISH command); thread/thread-paths.ts (threadScratchDir); thread/tools/index.ts.
- Test helpers: apps/api/test/helpers/thread-fixtures.ts:40-62 (seedThreadJobFor), sse-client.ts, migration-schema.ts (scratchSchemaBefore/applyMigration); route e2e coverage: apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts.

IMPACT / DEPENDENCY ORDER: US-001 is additive contract work (protocol union member + optional capability, API mirror, capability parsing, RunnerSummaryDto, ChatThreadRecord.projectId, mapThreadKind, repoThreadFields guard, Prisma index + migration 20261022090000_chat_thread_workspace, openapi regen). US-002 changes the repository signature (bare projectId -> ThreadScope) and owns every compile site (ThreadsService) so apps/api type-checks after it; it also hides WORKSPACE rows from every project thread surface (list/get/updateCap/command/archive/sendMessage/publish/discard + ThreadEventsGuard) and makes findThreadTokenScope return WORKSPACE. US-003 adds creation (validator, DTOs, WorkspaceThreadsService.create with home-project resolution, controller POST /threads, ThreadsModule imports ProjectsModule). US-004 adds read routes, commands, SSE events. US-005 adds send/archive and the session job target (jobTargetFor, sendRefusalFor, buildWorkspaceThreadInstructions). US-006 wires ASSIGN, placement misfit workspace_threads, git-token refusal, tool-route refusal, notices. US-007 (apps/runner) depends only on US-001.

RISKS: (1) Existing unit tests use kind 'WORKSPACE' as an 'unknown kind' fixture (chat-thread.domain.spec.ts:18-20, prisma-chat-thread.repository.spec.ts:219-222, prisma-fleet-job.repository.find-thread-assign.spec.ts:63-66); change to 'FUTURE' (cast as never where typed) in the story that changes the behavior. (2) Visibility leak: every shared repository lookup must filter by the scope fragment both pre-lock and under-lock inside sendMessage; publish/discard keep projectId but add kind {not:'WORKSPACE'}. (3) Do not inject PrismaService in WorkspaceThreadEventsGuard (api-data.md); read through WorkspaceThreadsService. (4) Project-scope reads must not leak through the events stream guard. (5) Generated files: run `bun run generate` from repo root for any API contract change; never hand-edit apps/cli/src/generated/ or openapi.json. (6) Every new controller route needs @ApiOperation/@ApiResponse, @ApiTags('fleet threads'), @ApiBearerAuth. (7) i18n: add `homeProjectAccess` to apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json. (8) Immutability: build new objects (e.g. attach homeProject via spread), do not mutate records. (9) No FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump; gated by workspaceThreads capability. (10) ThreadsModule importing ProjectsModule may need a stub in apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts for module specs. (11) apps/api tests need the compose test Postgres (`bun run test:db:up` in apps/api) for integration specs. (12) Budget gate keys use the home project and anchor repo for WORKSPACE turns, same as PROJECT.

RULINGS: S5b-R7, R9, R12, R13 (umbrella); 1d-D1 split, D2 creator-only incl. admins, D3 home project resolution, D4 workspaceThreads capability, D5 session job uses anchor repo/defaultBranch/feature thread-<threadId>, D6 no koda tools or project repos, D7 project surfaces never expose WORKSPACE, D8 no git token, D9 send re-checks home project, D10 ThreadScope. FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED kill switch applies unchanged.
outOfScope: Web pages for WORKSPACE threads (`/threads` list, new and detail pages, nav and command-palette entries): feature 1d-2 `fleet-s5b-workspace-tools`; this feature ships the API and the runner only.

koda tools in WORKSPACE threads — the `project` tool argument (S5b-R7), a per-kind descriptor catalog and the `koda_my_projects` tool — are feature 1d-2; a WORKSPACE session in this feature gets no koda tools and the runner tool route refuses its job.
Refusing a `project` argument on koda tools in REPO and PROJECT threads (S5b-R7) is feature 1d-2.
Project code mirrors or code tools for WORKSPACE threads: a WORKSPACE session never reads any repository.
ACP backends for WORKSPACE threads: refused at creation.
`write_doc`, Publish, Discard, Plan and Run for WORKSPACE threads: no `/threads/:id/publish`, `discard`, `plan` or `run` routes exist.
Visibility of WORKSPACE threads through any thread route to anyone but their creator, global admins included (S5b-R12, 1d-D2).
Changing a WORKSPACE thread's home project after creation, or converting a thread between kinds.

Hiding a WORKSPACE thread's THREAD job from the home project's job lists, job detail, job events, bundle route, dashboards, analytics, budgets or activity, or stopping the home project's job operators from cancelling it (S5b-R13 bookkeeping; none of these carries transcript text).
Changes to the job-log routes: a THREAD job's transcript is uploaded as the `thread` stream, which `LOG_STREAMS` never serves.
Hiding the home project's slug and name from the creator's own `/threads` responses after the creator leaves that project.
A database check constraint for the kind rule (1a-R4 still applies: the create paths enforce it).
A `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump; the additions are optional fields gated by the `workspaceThreads` capability.
Notifications, emails or activity feed entries specific to WORKSPACE threads.
Preserving WORKSPACE threads when their home project is hard-deleted: `ChatThread.project` cascades, as it does for every thread kind (projects are soft-deleted in normal operation).
A Playwright journey; this feature has no web change.
US-005 only: budget pauses scoped to the home project or its anchor repo also stop WORKSPACE threads; this coupling is accepted (S5b-R13).
US-005 only: a demotion that commits between the 1d-D9 host check and the send transaction is not detected for that one send.
US-003 only: rate limiting of `POST /threads` beyond the API's global throttler.
